summary: Tears down the career-mode player stats display: frees the stat linked list rooted at this+0x44, clears list bookkeeping, repopulates the list with three stat keys (aCircuit, aExperienceLaps, aBestLap), runs state cleanup, rebuilds the player stats page via sub_469900, resets a flag via ByteSetterAt0xe0, and returns 0.

local_names.v2: linked-list cursor; this[17] head (this+0x44) then node next pointer
local_names.v5: per-node data object pointer read from node+0

operations.description: Walk the linked list starting at this+0x44: each node carries a data pointer at node+0, the next pointer at node+4, and a flag byte at node+8.
For flagged nodes free the inner string buffer and the node data object, then free every node wrapper, all through FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Clear the list bookkeeping fields this+0x44 (head), this+0x48 (tail), this+0x4C (count), this+0x50 (capacity) to 0.
Rebuild the stat list via LinkedListInsertWithNodeAllocation with key -1: aCircuit, aExperienceLaps, aBestLap.
StateCleanupNotification(this): notify state machinery that the display was torn down.
sub_469900(this): rebuild the player stats display page from the remaining data.
ByteSetterAt0xe0(0): reset a flag byte associated with the display.

unresolved: The semantic meaning of the per-node flag byte and the player-stats key labels is carried from corpus names only; the display mapping is not verified
Only three stat keys are reinstated here versus the thirteen reinstated by the analogous career driver stats reset function; whether the player stats page intentionally shows fewer rows is unresolved
